lastReleaseMessage: the version pill and the changelog catch up with what is deployed

milestone.label: v0.16 - Supabase auth + Stripe subscriptions + live TICA data pipeline

items: RE-COUNTED 2026-09-02 against the same eight gates and HELD at 84, because no gate moved. The counting rule is written down here so the next audit can re-derive the number in a minute instead of asking the question a fourth time: each of the eight version-one gates in the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md is worth 12.5 points, a gate scores full when it is shipped, and a gate whose code is finished but whose last step is a ruling or a reading nobody has taken yet scores partial. Six gates are shipped, so the floor is 75. The two open gates, the free-tier measurement and the billing enforcement flag, are both code-complete with one non-code step left each, so the defensible band runs from 75 at no credit to 87.5 at half credit, and 84 sits inside it. What happened since the 2026-08-26 anchor is repair work on gates that were already counted, not a gate closing: v0.18.0 fixed a Stripe webhook that had answered 500 on every delivery since the event log landed, migration 0012 granted back the execute permission migration 0009 revoked, and v0.18.1 made the audit trail say so when its durable write fails. The billing gate is in better shape than it was on the anchor date and still is not enforcing, so the number stays where it is. Moving it needs a gate to close.

RE-COUNTED 2026-08-26 against an approved scope, which is why the number finally moved. It sat at 76 through three reviews because the completion question could not be answered while the freeze-versus-phase-two decision was open: a percentage needs a denominator, and there was not one. Kane ruled keep building, under a no-cost-increase constraint, and the scope is now eight gates written into the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md. Six of the eight are shipped. Three of them closed today in v0.17.36: data stewardship (export, erasure, retention policy, public retention page), durability (the community judge ratings now have a daily Postgres snapshot, migration 0010, and were the last dataset with no second copy), and the code half of running inside the free tier. Four surfaces moved out of the count entirely rather than being finished, and that is a real part of the change: the ten-table relational schema in 0001_init.sql is parked in the file itself, along with ownership certificate verification, the invite flow, and merged co-ownership. They were counting against completion while nobody intended to build them.
Billing gate: the Stripe subscription path is code-complete and one environment flag (SUBSCRIPTION_GATE_ENFORCE) from enforcing. Turning it on or deciding not to is the open gate.

Free-tier measurement: the write budget is now understood and the code is inside it, but nobody has read the actual key-value write counts off the Cloudflare dashboard. That reading needs an account token this session was not permitted to use, so the arithmetic in PROJECT_SPEC.md is unverified against real traffic.
Judge-panel coverage keeps converging by cron. Ongoing by design, not a gate that closes.

Security: view-as and shared-cats still read the key-value store rather than security-definer remote calls, so the two cross-account paths lack the database-enforced boundary that own-data reads have. Carried, not scoped as a version-one gate.

barRaise.reconcileNote: 2026-09-18 close reconciliation, both legs. Ten findings from the 2026-09-11 run were marked completed in the queue archive and each was re-read against the tree at 562be21 before closing: reliability-23, reliability-24, reliability-25, reliability-20, security-19, data-integrity-27, data-integrity-28, auth-token-hygiene-03, release-ps1-stack-04, compliance-data-steward-04. data-integrity-29 was NOT closed despite its queue row, because migration 0014 is on disk and unapplied, so the deployed prune is still the 0010 body; it moved to the deferred list instead. closedLog.evidence: an event type this app does not act on is stamped ignored rather than applied, through a new stripe_event_ignore function in migration 0013, so an ignored delivery stops raising the per-customer staleness watermark. Commit 490bb15, with a new webhook test and the migration probe updated to six guarded functions. Commit da90f1b then made the stamp survive a worker deployed ahead of its migration: a

handleUserDelete erases the durable copy first and aborts with 502 postgres_unavailable before touching any key-value store when that erasure is not confirmed, so an outage can no longer destroy the fast copy, the sharing grants and the vote markers while the durable account row survives. Commit 490bb15, with two new tests. Verified 2026-09-04 by running npm test in X:/YesAndRing: 144 of 144 pass.

handleStatePost reads the last written blob and skips both writes when the incoming state and name are unchanged under a stable serialization, reporting unchanged, and PROJECT_SPEC.md gains the write-volume row in the cost table.
